name: Why is the paint peeling in my bathroom?

mainEntity.name: Why is the paint peeling in my bathroom?

acceptedAnswer.text: Paint peeling in a bathroom is almost always caused by trapped moisture, inadequate ventilation, or poor surface prep before painting. If walls were painted over existing dust, grease, or peeling layers without sanding and priming, the bond fails. Similarly, taking hot showers without running an exhaust fan forces steam between paint layers and the drywall. In older homes across areas like Denver and Centennial, painting latex directly over old oil-based coatings without proper sanding and conversion primer frequently leads to sheet-like peeling.
acceptedAnswer.description: Peeling is caused by moisture buildup, lack of ventilation, painting over glossy or unprimed surfaces, or applying latex paint directly over oil paint.
